confidenceNote: These are the moves that actually shift each sub-stat, written plainly. They are directionally sound and deliberately not personalised — nothing here knows your situation, and none of it is advice. The effort and lift labels are honest rough estimates, not measurements.
note: Keyed by sub-stat id. `lift` is how much the move typically moves that one sub-stat: small, real, or big. `effort` is what it costs you: minutes, a weekend, or months. A move that is big AND minutes is rare and always listed first.

incomePower.do: Find out what your job actually pays elsewhere
incomePower.how: Three job ads and one honest conversation with someone who left. Most people are wrong about their own market rate, and always in the same direction.

incomePower.do: Ask for the number, once, out loud
incomePower.how: The single most reliable way to raise this. It is uncomfortable for about ninety seconds and then it is done.
Changing employer still moves pay more than staying and being excellent does. Unfair, well documented, worth knowing.

incomeTrajectory.do: Get the next title, not the next raise
incomeTrajectory.how: Titles reset the band you are paid inside. A raise moves you within it.

incomeTrajectory.do: Pick one skill your industry is short of and get visibly good at it
incomeTrajectory.how: Visibly is the load-bearing word. Nobody pays for a skill they cannot see.
Two of those in a row is a pay cut wearing a nice hat.

hustleCapacity.do: Earn one pound outside your job
hustleCapacity.how: Genuinely one. The gap between zero and one is the whole thing; everything after is volume.

hustleCapacity.do: Name the thing you would do if the job vanished on Friday
hustleCapacity.how: Having an answer is most of the score. Not having one is the risk.

hustleCapacity.do: Turn something you already do for free into something someone pays for
hustleCapacity.how: Lowest-friction second income there is: no new skill, just an invoice.

liquidityAgility.do: Move some of it somewhere you can actually reach
liquidityAgility.how: Money locked behind a penalty is not available in the week you need it, which is the only week that counts.

liquidityAgility.do: Open a separate account and stop looking at it
liquidityAgility.how: Separation beats willpower. It also stops your buffer being spent by accident.

liquidityAgility.do: Check what your investments cost to sell in a hurry
liquidityAgility.how: Some are same-day. Some are not. Find out on a calm afternoon, not on a bad Tuesday.

structuralMobility.how: A verbal arrangement is worth nothing the day your manager changes.

structuralMobility.do: Do not sign a longer lease than you need
structuralMobility.how: Every extra month is a month you cannot take a better offer somewhere else.

structuralMobility.do: Work out what it would actually cost to move
structuralMobility.how: Usually far less than the imagination says, and knowing the number makes the option real.

obligationFlex.do: List every payment that leaves whether you like it or not
obligationFlex.how: Write them down. The list is always longer than the memory of it.

obligationFlex.do: Kill the largest fixed cost you can live without
obligationFlex.how: One big cut beats six small ones and you only have to be brave once.

obligationFlex.do: Refinance anything above about seven percent
obligationFlex.how: The rate is the wound. The balance is only the size of it.

savingsRate.do: Automate it on payday, before you see it
savingsRate.how: You cannot spend what never arrived. This one move does more than every budgeting app combined.

savingsRate.do: Save the whole of your next raise
savingsRate.how: You are already living without it, so it costs nothing to lose and it compounds forever.
One percent is invisible in a month and enormous over twenty years. Then do it again next year.

consistency.how: Consistency is not discipline, it is automation plus time. Set it up once and let the calendar do the work.

consistency.do: Pick a rate you can hold in a bad month, not a good one
consistency.how: A rate you abandon in March scores worse than a smaller one you never break.

consistency.do: Keep going through one genuinely rough patch
consistency.how: This is the only way this score gets past its cap. It cannot be bought or hurried.

reserveDepth.do: Get to one month of spending, then stop worrying about the rest for now
reserveDepth.how: The first month removes most of the panic. Everything after is refinement.

reserveDepth.do: Work out what one month of your life actually costs
reserveDepth.how: Most people guess low by a third, which makes their buffer a third too small.

reserveDepth.do: Point one windfall at it and finish the job
reserveDepth.how: A bonus, a refund, a birthday. This is the one thing a windfall is unambiguously good at.

taxLiteracy.do: Find out your actual effective rate
taxLiteracy.how: Not the top band — the real share of everything you earned. Almost everyone is surprised.

taxLiteracy.do: Learn the accounts your country lets you use, and their limits
taxLiteracy.how: There is a short list. Knowing it is worth more per hour than almost anything else on this page.

taxLiteracy.do: Check whether you are leaving an allowance unused this year
taxLiteracy.how: Most allowances do not roll over. They expire quietly and nobody writes to tell you.

marketLiteracy.do: Look up what happened in 2000, 2008 and 2020
marketLiteracy.how: Not to predict anything. So that the next one feels like weather rather than the end of the world.

marketLiteracy.do: Learn the difference between an index and a fund that tracks one
marketLiteracy.how: This single distinction saves people more money than any stock pick ever made them.

marketLiteracy.do: Find out what you are paying in fees, as a number
marketLiteracy.how: A percent sounds small. Say it as pounds a year over thirty years and it stops sounding small.

instrumentLiteracy.do: Be able to say what each thing you own actually is
instrumentLiteracy.how: Out loud, in one sentence, without looking. Anything that fails this test is worth an hour.

instrumentLiteracy.do: Read one page of the terms on your largest holding
instrumentLiteracy.how: Just one. Usually the fees page. It is the one they hope you skip.

instrumentLiteracy.do: Learn what happens to each of them if you need the money in a hurry
instrumentLiteracy.how: Penalty, delay, or loss. Three very different answers and most people do not know which is which.

scenarioForesight.do: Write down what you would do if your income stopped on Friday
scenarioForesight.how: Three lines. The writing is the exercise — a plan you have never said out loud is not a plan.

scenarioForesight.do: Price the thing you are quietly dreading
scenarioForesight.how: Dread survives on vagueness. A number is almost always less frightening than the fog was.

scenarioForesight.do: Ask what has to be true for this to go wrong, before you commit

selfAwareness.do: Read your last month of spending without defending any of it
selfAwareness.how: The defending is the part that stops it working. Just look.

selfAwareness.do: Name the one purchase you always regret
selfAwareness.how: Everyone has exactly one pattern. Naming it removes most of its power.

selfAwareness.do: Notice which feeling comes before the spending
selfAwareness.how: It is nearly always the same one, and it is nearly never about money.

threatDetection.do: Learn the two or three shapes a scam takes
threatDetection.how: Urgency, secrecy, and a guaranteed return. Almost all of them are one of these wearing a costume.

threatDetection.do: Add a rule that nothing gets decided the same day it is pitched
threatDetection.how: Time is the one thing every bad offer cannot survive.

threatDetection.do: Check what would actually happen if your details leaked tomorrow
threatDetection.how: Knowing your own blast radius is most of the defence.

negotiation.do: Ask one company for a better rate this week
negotiation.how: Insurance, broadband, anything. Practise on something small so the big one is not your first attempt.

negotiation.do: Say the number and then stop talking
negotiation.how: The silence after is the whole technique. Most people fill it and negotiate against themselves.

negotiation.do: Find out what the other side actually needs
negotiation.how: Often it is not money. Often it is something you can give away cheaply.

network.do: Message one person you have not spoken to in a year
network.how: No agenda. Almost every well-paid opportunity arrives through a weak tie rather than a close one.

network.do: Be publicly findable for the thing you are good at
network.how: One page, one profile, one sentence. Opportunity cannot reach a person it cannot see.

network.do: Help someone with no expectation of return
network.how: The most reliable long-run investment on this entire page, and the only one with no downside.

personability.do: Ask more questions than you answer, once, deliberately
personability.how: People decide how they feel about you by how they felt talking to you.

personability.do: Follow up when you said you would
personability.how: Almost nobody does. The bar is on the floor and stepping over it is remembered for years.

personability.do: Learn to say the awkward thing kindly and early
personability.how: Every difficult conversation gets more expensive the longer it is left.
